name: SIM Card Swap
description:
Adversaries may gain access to mobile devices through transfers or swaps from victims’ phone numbers to adversary-controlled SIM cards and mobile devices.(Citation: ATT SIM Swap Scams)(Citation: Verizon SIM Swapping) 

The typical process is as follows:  

1. Adversaries will first gather information about victims through [Phishing](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1660), social engineering, data breaches, or other avenues. 
2. Adversaries will then impersonate victims as they contact mobile carriers to request for the SIM swaps. For example, adversaries would provide victims’ name and address to mobile carriers; once authenticated, adversaries would request for victims’ phone numbers to be transferred to adversary-controlled SIM cards.  
3. Once completed, victims will lose mobile data, such as text messages and phone calls, on their mobile devices. In turn, adversaries will receive mobile data that was intended for the victims.  

Adversaries may use the intercepted SMS messages to log into online accounts that use SMS-based authentication. Specifically, adversaries may use SMS-based authentication to log into banking and/or cryptocurrency accounts, then transfer funds to adversary-controlled wallets.

references.description: AT&T. (n.d.). UPDATE: Secure Your Number to Reduce SIM Swap Scams. Retrieved January 27, 2025.

telemetry.name: Host Status
telemetry.description: Host health and availability observations such as heartbeat, shutdown or degraded state.
telemetry.collection_focus: Collect agent heartbeat and OS health independently; record missed polls, last-seen time and monitor health.

providers.name: osquery
providers.scope: Scheduled host-state queries; supported tables and privileges vary by OS. Select a table that actually exposes the required object.

providers.name: Linux Audit plus inventory snapshots
providers.scope: Events explain changes; snapshots describe state at collection time.

configuration: Define the inventory query, allowed host set, interval and least-privileged reader. Store a stable asset ID, observation time and collector version.
Keep successive snapshots and calculate additions, removals and changed attributes. Pair state changes with audit events when available.
Export collector health and missed-poll counts so a missing snapshot is not misclassified as a missing asset.
telemetry.example_note: Project-normalized synthetic JSON, not a native provider log, captured event, attack verdict or validated detection. A parser/adapter is required for a real SIEM. Example names, IPs and values are fictional.
telemetry.limitations: Snapshots miss short-lived objects and do not identify who caused a change. A generic inventory agent is not guaranteed to expose firmware or kernel-level details.
telemetry.anomaly_design: Compare authorized state snapshots: first-seen drivers/services/modules, unexpected configuration drift and integrity changes. Record collection cadence; absence in a sample is not evidence of deletion.

telemetry.name: System Settings
telemetry.description: Mobile system-setting state or changes exposed to the collector.
telemetry.collection_focus: Use supported settings/service snapshots before and after the lab action; record scope (device/user/profile) and unavailable settings.

providers.name: Android logcat
providers.scope: Permitted logs from a consented test device/emulator; output depends on build, permissions and instrumentation.

providers.name: Android dumpsys
providers.scope: Point-in-time service/package state on an authorized development device.

providers.name: Instrumented test application
providers.scope: Own-app permission, API and state callbacks; not universal visibility into other apps.

configuration: Use a disposable emulator or owned development device with approved debugging. Record OS/API level, app version and instrumentation privileges.
Collect only relevant logcat buffers/tags and service snapshots; add explicit own-app instrumentation for events absent from OS logs.
Forward sanitized logs and compare before/after state. Remove test data and revoke debugging access after the lab session.
telemetry.example_note: Project-normalized synthetic JSON, not a native provider log, captured event, attack verdict or validated detection. A parser/adapter is required for a real SIEM. Example names, IPs and values are fictional.
telemetry.limitations: Android tooling does not imply iOS coverage. Standard mobile apps cannot observe all other apps or protected OS internals; MDM status is not full API, filesystem or content telemetry.
telemetry.anomaly_design: Per owned device, app version and permission state: unexpected API/permission changes, background activity and network destinations. OS privacy restrictions and emulator differences limit observability.

telemetry.name: User Account Authentication
telemetry.description: Authentication attempts and outcomes for a user or workload account.
telemetry.collection_focus: Collect successful and failed sign-ins, authentication method, application and conditional-access context; distinguish account validation from session creation.

providers.name: Microsoft Entra sign-in logs
providers.scope: Interactive, non-interactive and workload sign-in contexts, subject to tenant features and access.

providers.name: Cloud identity service audit
providers.scope: Issuer-side credential and administrative events where the service supports them.

providers.name: Application audit instrumentation
providers.scope: Application-side use of identities and sessions; design fields without raw tokens.

configuration: Enable/export the required identity sign-in and audit categories from the lab tenant to a protected destination. Document license, role and retention requirements.
Correlate issuance or administrative changes with later sign-ins using non-secret credential IDs, application IDs, user IDs and correlation IDs.
Exclude passwords, bearer tokens, cookies and private keys. Record success, failure, authentication context and application result separately.
telemetry.example_note: Project-normalized synthetic JSON, not a native provider log, captured event, attack verdict or validated detection. A parser/adapter is required for a real SIEM. Example names, IPs and values are fictional.
telemetry.limitations: A token creation record is not evidence of token use; a sign-in is not a complete record of every resource access. Some provider-side data is unavailable to the customer.
telemetry.anomaly_design: Per identity and application: first-seen clients/resources, changes in authentication failures and session patterns, and unusual permission changes. Separate automation, travel, shared egress and identity-provider policy changes.

analytics.name: Analytic 1747
analytics.guidance: For Android, detect SIM Card Swap by correlating analyst-visible device/network evidence and management state; use streaming or batched telemetry only where the documented collector is deployed. Correlate Host Status via Android Enterprise DPC [DevicePolicyManager policy/compliance/security-state queries and SecurityLog events where supported]; System Settings via Android Enterprise DPC [DevicePolicyManager policy/compliance/security-state queries and SecurityLog events where supported]; User Account Authentication via Application Vetting / Identity Provider Telemetry [App authentication flow instrumentation or IdP sign-in/audit events]. Alert on a sequence or state change inconsistent with the device/app baseline, approved management policy, or expected user workflow; do not infer unobserved API calls, file/process activity, or payload content from management state alone.

tuning.description: Default 300s service loss. Brief outages are normal; sustained loss + ICCID change is anomalous.

mitigations.name: User Guidance
mitigations.description: The user should become familiar with social engineering tactics that ask for Personally Identifiable Information (PII). Additionally, the user should include the use of hardware tokens, biometrics, and other non-SMS based authentication mechanisms where possible. Finally, the user should enable SIM swapping protections offered by the mobile carrier, such as setting up a PIN or password to authorize any changes to the account.

mitigations.name: Enterprise Policy
mitigations.description: Enterprises should monitor for SIM card changes on the Enterprise Mobility Management (EMM) or the Mobile Device Management (MDM).

simulation.prerequisites: Use owned test devices or emulators, disposable app accounts and test data. Verify platform/version instrumentation; desktop test procedures do not establish mobile coverage.
